title: What Earth's horizon costs
summary: At the south pole Earth sits low on the horizon and ridges hide it. With direct links only, the base delivers {{r:dte_loss}} less cargo a year, mostly because one work site never sees Earth. A part-time relay or more autonomy fixes it; more rovers do not.
notes: E21 (experiments/phase4/run_phase4.py, analysis experiments/phase4/analyse_e21.py): P2 six-rover fleet, marketplace, pads 1 km, no plume, 20 seeds per cell, start years 2028-2031. Wording by LEAD, 22 Oct 2026.

always_t.label: Delivered with Earth always in view
always_t.note: Earth always in view, all supervised rovers, strict policy (E21 stage A)

dte_loss.label: Lost against Earth always in view

base_link.label: Time Earth is in view at the base
base_link.note: share of 2028-2031 in which any part of Earth's disc is above the terrain horizon at the base, 2.5 m antenna (B-40)

isru_lost.label: ISRU cargo never delivered
isru_lost.note: cargo bound for the ISRU plant that is never delivered under direct links only (E21 analysis)

dte_wait.label: Rover time spent waiting for Earth
dte_wait.note: rover time spent waiting for Earth in the year

relay_t.label: Delivered, relay a tenth of the time
relay_t.note: a relay satellite in view a tenth of the time, besides direct links

auto_t.label: Delivered by autonomous rovers
auto_t.note: direct links only, fully autonomous rovers

rover_gain.label: Gain from one extra supervised rover
rover_gain.note: gain of one extra supervised LTV over direct links only (E21 stage B)

half_strict.label: Half relay: one in ten urgent waits over
half_strict.note: urgent cargo: hours within which 90 % is delivered, relay in view half the time, strict supervision (E21 stage B)

half_plus1.label: The same with one extra rover
half_plus1.note: the same with one extra rover

half_strategic.label: The same with strategic driving
half_strategic.note: the same with supervised rovers that drive between check-ins on their own (strategic policy)

rover_dp.label: Relay coverage worth one extra rover
rover_dp.note: relay coverage that gives the same urgent delay as one extra rover, at half coverage (bootstrap over seeds)

strategic_dp.label: Relay coverage worth strategic driving
strategic_dp.note: relay coverage that gives the same urgent delay as the strategic policy, at half coverage

steps.title: Earth hangs on the horizon
steps.text: Seen from the south pole Earth never climbs high, and ridges hide it. From the base it is in view {{r:base_link}} of the time. A rover driven or supervised from Earth needs that link.
steps.visual: Earth low over the ridge; the terrain shadow marks where it is hidden.

steps.title: Waiting for Earth
steps.text: With direct links only, rovers spend {{r:dte_wait}} a year parked, waiting for Earth to rise.
steps.visual: Rovers parked in the waiting colour while Earth is below the ridge.

steps.title: The cargo it costs
steps.text: The base delivers {{r:dte_t}} instead of {{r:always_t}}: {{r:dte_loss}} less.
steps.visual: The delivery counter of the year, with and without the horizon.

steps.title: One site never sees Earth
steps.text: Most of that loss is one place. The plant that makes oxygen from regolith sits where Earth is never in view, so {{r:isru_lost}} of cargo for it never arrives. No rover driven from Earth can work there.
steps.visual: The ISRU site highlighted; its route drawn in the colour for no link.

steps.title: A relay, or autonomy
steps.text: A relay satellite in view only a tenth of the time brings deliveries back to {{r:relay_t}}. Fully autonomous rovers reach {{r:auto_t}} with no relay at all.
steps.visual: A relay link drawn from the rovers to a satellite passing over.

steps.title: More rovers cannot buy it back
steps.text: One more supervised rover adds {{r:rover_gain}}: it waits for Earth like the others.
steps.visual: The fleet with an extra rover, parked in the waiting colour.

steps.title: Autonomy is worth more than a rover
steps.text: With a relay in view half the time, nine in ten urgent items arrive within {{r:half_strict}}. One more rover brings that to {{r:half_plus1}}. Letting supervised rovers drive on their own between check-ins brings it to {{r:half_strategic}}. In relay terms the rover is worth {{r:rover_dp}} and the autonomy step {{r:strategic_dp}}.
steps.visual: Three bars: the fleet as it is, one more rover, and the autonomy step.
